title: InfraTrust report warns of exploited flaws in critical network infrastructure
summary: Hackers are actively exploiting security flaws in network devices like firewalls and VPNs using a technique called "PHP2Shell". This puts critical business web management tools at serious risk of compromise.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses these network appliances, your IT team should check the InfraTrust report and secure the management interfaces.

title: Hackers Target Critical Oracle E-Business Suite RCE Flaw Days After Security Patch
summary: Hackers are actively scanning the internet for a critical security flaw in Oracle E-Business Suite just days after a patch was released. This matters because unpatched systems can be remotely taken over by attackers.

also_covered.title: Hackers now scanning systems for recently-patched Oracle flaw

action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses Oracle E-Business Suite, your IT team should already be applying the latest security updates.
action_it: Apply Oracle's Critical Patch Update immediately to fix CVE-2026-101767 and monitor systems for unauthorized probing or access attempts.

title: Adobe Fixes 8 Critical Campaign Classic Flaws Allowing Code Execution and Security Bypass
summary: Adobe released security patches for eight critical vulnerabilities in Campaign Classic that could allow attackers to run unauthorized code or bypass security controls. Fixing these flaws is important to protect enterprise systems from being taken over.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses Adobe Campaign Classic, your IT team should apply these updates.
action_it: Apply Adobe's patches for the eight fixed flaws in Campaign Classic as soon as possible.

title: CISA warns of hackers now exploiting critical Node2Shell flaw
summary: Hackers are now actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in a software component known as Node2Shell. This flaw allows attackers to compromise systems, making it urgent to secure affected environments.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your organization uses this software, your IT team needs to take action immediately.
action_it: Review guidance from the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and apply available updates or mitigations for the Node2Shell flaw immediately.

title: Critical 16-Year-Old UEFI Flaw Can Run Code Before Secure Boot on Network-Booting Servers
summary: A 16-year-old flaw in widely used computer boot software allows attackers to run malicious code before the operating system starts. This affects servers that boot up using a network connection.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything, as this affects servers that boot over a network rather than home computers.
action_it: Apply security updates for EDK II from your hardware vendor and restrict network-booting environments to trusted networks until patches are installed.

title: American Organizations Under Attack: Skyw4lker Device Code Phishing Campaign Exposed
summary: A phishing campaign called Skyw4lker is targeting American organizations using device codes to gain unauthorized access to corporate accounts. It matters because attackers are abusing legitimate cloud services and authentication methods to slip in undetected.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses the targeted cloud services, your IT team should already be monitoring for unauthorized device logins.
action_it: Review authentication logs for suspicious device code login attempts and educate users on recognizing advanced phishing campaigns that abuse legitimate cloud workflows.

title: Japan's GMO Offers $1 Million Bounty to Catch Hackers Behind FX Trading Cloud Breach
summary: Japanese internet company GMO is offering a $1 million reward for tips leading to the arrest of hackers who breached its cloud service and demanded a ransom. Customers using the service have been urged to shut down their computers and disconnect from the internet to avoid a potential ransomware attack.

also_covered.title: Japan's GMO urges customers to shut down PCs amid ransomware threat

action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you use GMO's Onamae Desktop Cloud service for FX trading, disconnect your computer from the internet and shut it down immediately as advised by the company.

title: Tailscale Patches SSH Flaws That Could Let Hacked Devices Gain Root Access on Other Servers
summary: Tailscale has patched security flaws in its built-in SSH server that could allow compromised devices to gain top-level root access on other servers. This matters because an attacker could potentially reach sensitive files and services that should be heavily restricted.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you use Tailscale for personal or business connections, update your software to version 1.104.4 as soon as possible.
action_it: Apply Tailscale version 1.104.4 immediately to fix the SSH forwarding flaws.

title: ShinyHunters-Exploited Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day Turns Out to Be Three Chained Flaws
summary: Attackers exploited three chained security flaws in Oracle PeopleSoft software starting in May. Oracle released a patch for the vulnerabilities in June under the identifier CVE-2026-35273.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses Oracle PeopleSoft, your IT team should already be on it.
action_it: Apply Oracle's patches associated with CVE-2026-35273 and check systems for signs of compromise.

title: Microsoft urges Entra ID admins to migrate users to passkeys
summary: Microsoft is urging administrators to move users away from text message and phone call sign-ins before they are retired in February 2027. Making this change helps prevent future sign-in problems and protects accounts from being stolen by trickery.

title: Even after PHP2Shell, blast radius matters more than a CVSS score
summary: Attackers can quickly exploit software vulnerabilities before organizations have time to apply patches. Experts recommend limiting the access permissions of accounts and digital tools to reduce potential damage if a breach occurs.

title: Wazuh and AI for Enhanced SOC Workflows
summary: An article discusses how artificial intelligence is being used to improve security operations centers and automate tasks. It highlights the growing role of AI in defending against cyber threats.

title: Nefilim and Hive ransomware affiliate gets 70 months in prison
summary: A Ukrainian national was sentenced to nearly six years in prison for his role in ransomware attacks against hospitals and government entities. The sentencing brings a measure of justice to victims of major cyberattacks that disrupted critical services worldwide.

title: Anthropic's Unreleased AI Model Chains Flaws Into Working Chrome, Safari, Windows and Linux Exploits
summary: An unreleased Anthropic artificial intelligence model successfully found and chained multiple security flaws in major operating systems and browsers to create working proof-of-concept exploits in a lab. Because Anthropic reported the flaws responsibly, all of them have already been patched by the respective vendors.

title: FBI Seizes Virtualine Domain Over Alleged Criminal Hosting and Bitcoin Money Laundering
summary: The U.S. government seized the domain for a hosting company that allowed criminals to hide online. The service was used for serious crimes, including sharing explicit images without consent and laundering money.
